name: Chirisa Technology Parks

profile.reading:
The Piscataway, New Jersey campus operated by Chirisa Technology Parks sits at 201 Centennial Avenue in Middlesex County, roughly midway between New York City and Philadelphia, and the company positions it as an interconnection hub for enterprise and carrier customers across the New York/New Jersey/Philadelphia corridor. Public reporting from Chirisa and its affiliated colocation operator, Digital Fortress, traces the site's history in stages rather than as one clean narrative: an existing building on the property, addressed as 201B Centennial Avenue and roughly 96,559 square feet, was already operating as a data center by 2019 under Digital Fortress management, offering just over 4 MW of capacity to roughly a dozen customers, anchored by a long-term contract with a major global carrier. In 2024, Chirisa Technology Parks took over that facility from Digital Fortress and disclosed plans to grow site-wide power at Piscataway toward 25 MW, starting with a 12 MW build-out for a large customer.

Chirisa's more recent public materials describe an expanded, roughly 20-acre Piscataway campus with two buildings referred to internally as PNJ-01 and PNJ-02, combining adaptive reuse of the existing structure with new, greenfield construction, and a company target of reaching 90 MW of power across the campus by mid-2026, with the newer PNJ-02 building's delivery reserved for 2027. That 90 MW figure is a company-stated, campus-wide planning target rather than a confirmed, currently operating load, and Chirisa has not published a building-by-building breakdown clarifying how much of that capacity sits in the older adaptive-reuse structure versus the new construction.

What the public record does not include is independently confirmed detail on tenancy beyond the single named anchor carrier, on the building's construction specifics such as raised-floor area, cooling architecture, or redundancy tier, or on progress against the 2024 and 2027 milestones as of this writing. Terms of the 2024 internal transaction between Chirisa and Digital Fortress were explicitly not disclosed in trade coverage. As a privately held real estate and colocation operator, Chirisa is under no obligation to publish granular facility specifications, and its public disclosures read as marketing and investor-relations material aimed at prospective tenants and partners rather than a full technical profile of the Piscataway asset. Readers should treat the 90 MW campus figure as a stated ambition to watch for delivery against, not a confirmed operating capacity.
profile.research_note: Chirisa's own site states the Piscataway NJ campus (20 acres, two facilities PNJ-01 and PNJ-02, adaptive reuse plus new greenfield build) will reach 90MW of power by mid-2026, with PNJ-02 reserved for 2027 delivery. Figure is campus-wide across both buildings, not confirmed per-building; stored as planned since not yet fully operating.

reading:
Chirisa Technology Parks is a privately held developer of hyperscale, high performance computing and AI data centre campuses, working through both adaptive reuse of existing buildings and greenfield construction. Its own site does not publish a corporate headquarters address, but the Piscataway tax roll effectively does. The entity that owns its New Jersey asset gives its mailing address as 1401 Meadowville Technology Parkway, Chester, Virginia, which is the company's Richmond area campus in Chesterfield County.

The company describes a Richmond campus of 230 acres and 534,000 square feet targeted at 360 MW of power by the end of 2026, a 50 acre Chicago campus of 200,000 square feet with 28 MW of utility power, a Lynnwood, Washington adaptive reuse site with 13 MW of utility power available, a 20 acre Piscataway campus targeted at 90 MW of power by mid 2026, and a 150 acre Lancaster, Pennsylvania campus spread across two sites of roughly 75 acres each. It claims more than 850,000 square feet operational and a United States pipeline in excess of one gigawatt. Every one of those megawatt figures is either utility power or a forward target. None of them is stated as critical IT load, and they should not be read as one.

Capital has arrived alongside the announcements. In August 2025 Blue Owl Capital, Chirisa and Machine Investment Group closed four billion dollars of funding for previously announced CoreWeave developments at Lancaster, with Blue Owl stating an intention to fund up to twenty billion dollars of Chirisa developments, and with the parties intending to fund roughly 200 million dollars of local grid improvements in partnership with PPL Electric Utilities. Chirisa says the partnership currently supports almost half a gigawatt of new development underway in Virginia and Pennsylvania.

The single facility this registry holds for Chirisa is in New Jersey, and the county record is more precise than the marketing. Piscataway Township block 6702, lot 3.03 is 201 Centennial Avenue, a two unit condominium over a building dating to 1972. Unit C0001 is owned by Landmark Digital Infrastructure OP of El Segundo, California, recorded at 22.5 million dollars on 1 December 2020. Unit C0002 is owned by CTP 201 Centennial LLC, recorded at 11 million dollars on 19 November 2025. Chirisa therefore owns one of two condominium units at that address, and a separate digital infrastructure owner holds the other. The 90 MW figure is a stated ambition across the whole 20 acre site and both planned buildings, not an operating load in the unit Chirisa bought, and the mid 2026 date attached to it has now passed without a published delivery confirmation.

The registry row is OpenStreetMap relation 2744301, which carried the name Verizon from August 2021 until 19 August 2026, when changeset 187668697 renamed it and added the Chirisa operator tag while updating names and building boundaries along Centennial Avenue. No Verizon owned parcel appears in the Piscataway assessment roll, so the earlier name looks like a mapper's local guess rather than a record of ownership, and the five year gap is a reminder that an operator name in this dataset can be years out of date in either direction.
